title: How to Lead Even When You Don't Know Where You Are Going
coreMove: Give directional clarity while naming uncertainty accurately and assigning the next move.
sourcePressure: Ambiguity is normal; leaders need psychological discipline, accurate confidence, behavioral consistency, and a message that names what is known, what is unknown, and who owns the next move.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version is confidence, calm presence, or vision when the leader lacks answers.

counterintuition: admit what you do not know

exampleSpecs.domain: regional blood bank during an unexplained test-equipment outage
exampleSpecs.audience: a director whose staff need immediate collection guidance before root cause is known
exampleSpecs.stakes: blood supply drops if collections stop, but unsafe testing cannot continue
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director states the confirmed outage, the unresolved root cause, and the next two-hour owner for manual verification before donor vans depart
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a testing analyzer with a fault code flashing beside labeled blood coolers

exampleSpecs.domain: regional ferry operator after a hull-sensor anomaly
exampleSpecs.audience: a port manager deciding whether to hold departures while engineers investigate
exampleSpecs.stakes: commuters need movement, but crews read every signal of leader anxiety
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager tells captains what the sensor proves, what inspection has not proved, and who will make the next departure call at 10:40
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a ferry departure board with one route blinking delayed

exampleSpecs.domain: online tax filing service during a possible calculation bug
exampleSpecs.audience: a support VP whose agents are inventing answers in live chats
exampleSpecs.stakes: false certainty could create legal exposure and customer panic
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the VP freezes improvised scripts, publishes a known-unknown-next-update note, and assigns one engineer to confirm the affected form set
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a live-chat dashboard filling with the same tax-form question

exampleSpecs.domain: produce co-op after a suspected pesticide drift report
exampleSpecs.audience: a co-op president balancing member farmers, buyers, and lab uncertainty
exampleSpecs.stakes: shipment decisions require action before lab confirmation returns
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the president asks members to predict buyer reaction to vague silence, then sends a bounded update with test timing and a hold decision for one lot
exampleSpecs.firstImage: sealed berry flats stacked beside a sample cooler

exampleSpecs.domain: architecture firm after a zoning reinterpretation threatens a hospital project
exampleSpecs.audience: a project principal whose designers need direction before the city issues final guidance
exampleSpecs.stakes: design work may need to change, but stopping everything wastes critical weeks
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the principal identifies the known zoning constraint, the uncertain ruling, and two design tracks with owners until the city meeting
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a marked-up zoning letter spread across hospital floor plans

exampleSpecs.domain: regional bank fraud desk during a new ATM skimming pattern
exampleSpecs.audience: a fraud director whose analysts want a full pattern before warning branches
exampleSpecs.stakes: waiting for certainty could cost customers, but overclaiming could trigger false alarms
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director writes a branch alert with verified transaction features, explicitly excludes unverified theories, and assigns a noon evidence review
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a fraud heat map with three ATM pins lit in yellow

skillTargets: distinguish honest confidence from fake certainty
identify behavioral signals that create decision drag
assign ownership under uncertainty without pretending the answer is complete

tryThisNowSpec: Write a three-line update for one uncertain situation: what is known, what is not known yet, and the next move with owner and time boundary.
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter
